summary: Recent discussions in the Spark community focus on extending Spark’s extensibility and improving developer experience.  The SPIP language‑agnostic UDF protocol and an external lookup join strategy are being proposed to enable UDFs to run outside the engine and to perform on‑demand joins with external storage.  Additionally, a fallback resolver for unknown V2 catalog names and a trial of automated AI code review for new pull requests are under consideration.

highlights.text: Proposal for SPIP, a unified API and execution protocol that allows user‑defined functions to run outside the Spark engine via IPC, aiming for consistent cross‑language support.

sources.title: SPIP: Language-agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark

highlights.text: Discussion of an external lookup join strategy that performs on‑demand lookups against external storage for the static side, eliminating the need to materialize it before the join.
Proposal of an optional fallback resolver that will be consulted when an application references a V2 catalog name that has not been pre‑configured in Spark.

sources.title: [DISCUSS][SQL] SPARK-59849: Fallback resolver for unknown V2 catalog names

highlights.text: Trial of automated AI code review using Claude for new Apache Spark pull requests, posting advisory comments without approvals.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Automated AI code review on new Spark PRs (trial)
